title: Three pointers keep four regions: small | equal | unexplored | large
caption: Here the array is partitioned around the pivot 5. The window is the unexplored region nums[mid .. high]. Everything left of low is < 5, low..mid−1 is == 5, and right of high is > 5.

frames.text: Start: everything is unexplored. low = mid = 0 and high = n − 1. nums[0] = 5 equals the pivot, so mid just moves on.
nums[mid] = 8 > 5: swap it with nums[high] and move high left. mid stays put, because the 3 that came back from the right hasn't been looked at yet.
nums[mid] = 3 < 5: swap it with nums[low], then move both low and mid right. What came from low was already explored (an equal value), so it's safe to step past it.
A few steps later, all four regions are visible: [3, 2] small, [5, 5] equal, [5, 1] unexplored, [9, 8] large.
mid passes high, so the unexplored region is empty and you're done, in one pass with O(1) extra space.
